grade.basis: Violin1 requires upper-register melody, rapid chromatic scale pickups including tuplets, articulate saltellato figures, and repeated high sixteenths at the Finale; lower parts also change between arco and pizzicato and include double stops. The concrete violin1 writing is early advanced rather than a virtuoso concertante part. The factual performance-floor hold is independent of this complete-score advisory grade.

findings.finding: Raw page168495 and actual complete Merton score82713 establish Quartet in E minor Op42 for four violins. Landscape booklet PDF contains printed scorepp3–15: IAllegro espressivo; IIScherzo Allegro assai / Trio più moderato; IIILarghetto; IVFinale Vivace.

Primary digital album credits J.Patrick Rafferty, violin, and groups the complete Op42 as19:50 with four tracks I7:53,II2:24,III5:50,IV3:41. Original four-violin work and each movement match complete notation; human whole-performance context independent of the incomplete YouTube example.
Album Jakob Dont (1815–1888), Quartets for Four Violins releasedMarch8,2023 under J.Patrick Rafferty,8tracks covering Op42 and Op45.

grade.basis: Violin1 needs secure shifting into upper ledger-line register and lyrical bow control, wide-leaping short strokes in the Scherzo, chromatic ornamental sixteenth/32nd-note figures in the slow Larghetto, and fluent eighth-note entries in the Vivace. Accompaniments are simpler but independent. Overall upper intermediate with a one-level margin; this is not inferred from Dont’s etude reputation or an automatic quartet surcharge.

scoreAnchors.location: Printedpp3–7/I; p8Scherzo mm1–40; pp9–11/Larghetto including mm25–40; pp11–15/Finale
scoreAnchors.observation: First movement mostly cantabile quarter/half-note material; Scherzo has accented octave/wider skips and detached quarters; slow movement decorative runs/accidentals; Finale moves in eighths with offbeat rests, chromatic shifts and recurring high-register attacks. All four movements inspected.
